faqs.question: How long should a Halloween card message for my girlfriend be?
faqs.answer: Match it to the card: about 12 words on a gift tag, 25 to 35 on a postcard back and 45 to 100 inside a folded card, by our estimates. If your draft runs past 55 words, pick a 5 × 7 card rather than a small A2 or A6 one.

faqs.question: What do I write in a Halloween card if we only just started dating?
faqs.answer: Keep it short and light: one thing you enjoy about her, a simple plan and an easy way to say no. Three or four sentences on a small card is plenty, and a gift-tag line on a treat is gentler still.

faqs.question: Can I mail a pop-up Halloween card as a postcard?
faqs.answer: No. Under USPS Domestic Mail Manual 101, a postcard must be unfolded, uncreased and evenly thick, so a folded pop-up never qualifies. Send it in an envelope from a post office counter, because a rigid or lumpy envelope can be treated as nonmachinable.

faqs.question: What is the biggest card I can send at the US postcard rate?
faqs.answer: DMM 101 sets the postcard range at 3½ × 5 inches to 4¼ × 6 inches, between 0.007 and 0.016 inch thick. Anything larger goes at letter rates, and its back gives you room for roughly 25 to 35 handwritten words.

faqs.question: What should a Halloween gift tag for her say?
faqs.answer: Twelve words or fewer that point at the gift or at her, such as "Open after dark, [name]." or "One treat, zero tricks. Love, me." Leave the longer feelings for a card or a page.

faqs.question: My girlfriend hates scary things. What Halloween card suits her?
faqs.answer: Choose a cute design such as a smiling pumpkin or a cartoon bat, and say in the message that the night will have no jump scares. Plan something cosy, like baking or a comfort film, and name it in the card.

faqs.question: How do I keep my handwriting straight on a plain card?
faqs.answer: Rule faint pencil lines 1 cm apart with a ruler, write over them, and erase only once the ink is fully dry. Test the pen on the envelope flap first, since felt tips can bleed into uncoated card.

faqs.question: Is a digital Halloween card okay instead of a paper one?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially if you are apart on 31 October or remembered late. Across SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, and a link has room for far more than a small card holds.

faqs.question: Can I add a voice note to a Halloween card for her?
faqs.answer: Paper cannot hold one, but the premium SubhSandesh Halloween page takes a voice note of up to 60 seconds plus up to 12 photos and a 3,000-character letter. It takes about 10 minutes to set up.

faqs.question: When is Halloween in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween is always 31 October, which is a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027. Post a paper card early that week so it arrives in time.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Card for Girlfriend: Messages Sized to Each Card Type

Halloween card for girlfriend, in one line: name one real moment between you and fit the space on the card, roughly 12 words on a gift tag, 25 to 35 on a postcard and 45 to 100 inside a folded card. Most people overshoot. The median letter written on SubhSandesh's "I miss you" template is 88 words (n=214, measured September 2026; a different template, not Halloween data), more than the inside of a small folded card holds.

When words won't fit on paper, a link has room, and 48.3% of SubhSandesh's shared pages are read on a phone. Below: a space table, 20 original Halloween card messages for a girlfriend, layout tips, a pop-up bat card to make and the cases where paper is the better choice. Halloween is Saturday 31 October in 2026 and Sunday 31 October in 2027.

## What should a Halloween card for your girlfriend say?

Say one specific thing, then stop. A 2026 study of [573 compliment letters sent to a Swiss neonatology team](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12911175) found a median length of only 47 words. The pile mixed cards and letters, handwritten and typed, yet writers still fitted in a remembered moment, their feelings and what they admired in the staff.

That gives a four-part recipe: a memory, a feeling, something you admire and a thank-you. In a [2021 diary study of 54 married couples over 14 days](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8053415), people felt more grateful on days they felt more supported by their partner, and less stressed. So thank her for one specific bit of support, though the study shows a link, not proof that a card changes anything.

Halloween cards have carried such notes for over a century. [The Public Domain Review's Halloween postcard collection](https://publicdomainreview.org/collection/halloween-postcards) dates the postcard's golden era to about 1905 to 1915, citing historian Lisa Morton's estimate of roughly 3,000 spooky designs.

## Which Halloween card type holds how many words?

Budgets below are our estimates for medium handwriting on pencil lines 1 cm apart. Postcard limits come from the [USPS Domestic Mail Manual 101](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/101.htm), and the last column sets each space against the 88-word median miss-you letter.

| Card type | Writing space (our estimate) | Word budget (our estimate) | Share of an 88-word median letter that fits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small folded card (US A2 or UK A6), inside right | About 7.5 × 11 cm, 11 lines | 45 to 55 words | About 60% |
| 5 × 7 inch folded card, inside right | About 10 × 15 cm, 15 lines | 90 to 100 words | All of it |
| Postcard back, message half (USPS card size tops out at 4¼ × 6 inches) | About 7 × 9 cm, 9 lines | 25 to 35 words | About 35% |
| Gift tag, or the strip under a pop-up | About 5 × 9 cm | 12 to 25 words | 15 to 30% |

If your draft reads like a letter, buy a 5 × 7 card or cut a third of it. A small folded card holds barely more than half of what people typically write.

## 20 Halloween card messages for your girlfriend, by card type

Every line here is new. Swap bracketed parts for your own details.

### 1. Inside a folded card: 45 to 100 words (3 messages)

The first suits a couple a year or more in. The second suits someone you have only just started seeing.

- Happy Halloween, [name]. Last October you laughed so hard on the haunted hayride that the guide stopped to check on you. I have replayed that sound more often than I will admit. This year I want the same plan: one properly scary thing, one hot drink, and your hand in mine all the way round.
- We have only known each other since [month], so this card is short and honest. You make plain weeknights feel like the opening chapter of something good, and I would like to read on. Will you spend Halloween with me? Costume optional, popcorn guaranteed.
- I know you would rather watch a baking show than a horror film, so that is the night I have planned. No jump scares, no masks at the door, just pumpkin bread that will probably sink in the middle. You make me braver than any film could.

### 2. Postcard back: 25 to 35 words (3 messages)

Anyone who handles a postcard can read it. Keep these warm rather than private.

- Report from the pumpkin patch: 212 pumpkins, one wobbly wheelbarrow, none as lovely as you. Wish you were here to choose the ugliest one with me.
- This card has travelled further than any sensible ghost would bother to. It carries one message: I miss you, and the last fun-size chocolate bar is yours.
- I counted 14 plastic skeletons on one street today. Not one of them grinned as wide as I do when your name lights up my phone.

### 3. Gift tag: 12 words or fewer (5 messages)

A tag sits on a present. It only needs to point at the gift or at her.

- Open after dark, [name].
- One treat, zero tricks. Love, me.
- To the one who out-screams every horror film.
- For your costume emergency kit.
- Careful: contains my whole heart and some caramel.

### 4. Pop-up card base: 15 to 25 words (3 messages)

The pop-up fills the middle. These sit on the strip underneath it.

- This bat flew out of the card to say one thing: I would follow you into any dark forest.
- Wings up, [name]. That is me every time you walk into a room.
- I cut, folded and glued this three times before it stood up. You were worth every crooked attempt.

### 5. Fill-in-the-blank lines for any card (6 messages)

These follow the four-part recipe. Combine two or three of them to fill a folded card.

- My favourite memory of us this year is [one moment]. I still grin about it.
- You looked [adjective] as a [her costume], but you look even better as yourself.
- Thank you for [something kind she did lately]. It carried me through [the week].
- If I were a ghost, I would haunt [a place you both love], in case you came back.
- The scariest part of this October was [a real worry], and you shrank it.
- I knew I was in trouble the day you [small habit of hers].

## Handwriting and layout: 6 tips for a neat card

Most card mistakes happen in the first ten seconds of ink. All six need only a pen, a pencil and a ruler.

- Draft the message on your phone first and check its word count against the table.
- Rule faint pencil guides 1 cm apart with a ruler, and rub them out only once the ink is fully dry.
- Try your pen on the inside of the envelope flap, since felt tips can bleed into uncoated card.
- On black or deep purple card, switch to a white or metallic gel pen.
- If the message runs under 30 words, begin about a third of the way down so it sits centred.
- When a word goes wrong, draw a tiny bat or spider over it instead of starting again.

## How to make a pop-up bat card in about 25 minutes

A V-fold is a folded shape glued at an angle across the centre crease, so it rises as the card opens. You need A4 or US Letter cardstock, black paper, scissors, glue and a ruler; 25 minutes is our first-try estimate.

1. Fold the cardstock in half to make an A5 or 5½ × 8½ inch card.
2. Draw a bat about 10 cm from wingtip to wingtip on the black paper and cut it out.
3. Fold the bat in half down its body, head to tail.
4. Fold a 1 cm tab under the bottom edge of each wing, angled away from the body crease.
5. Glue the tabs inside the card, bat crease on card crease, and hold for 30 seconds.
6. Close the card gently and trim any wingtip that pokes past the edge.
7. Write a 15-to-25-word line from section 4 on the strip below the bat.

Hand it over or post it in an envelope at a counter. Under DMM 101, a card only qualifies as a postcard if it is unfolded, uncreased, evenly thick and no more than 0.016 inch thick, and an envelope that is too rigid or lumpy counts as nonmachinable.

## Sending the card as a Halloween page instead

A link suits a girlfriend in another city, or a card remembered on 30 October. Both SubhSandesh Halloween templates are built for one recipient, with a partner mode.

The [interactive Halloween card where she carves your pumpkin](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about 5 minutes to set up. She knocks three times, carves until your word lights, reads your letter by torchlight in the attic and finds up to six photos before the boo question, and you hear by email once she answers. The [premium Halloween website with your voice and a countdown](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about 10 minutes and adds a voice clip of up to a minute, 12 photos, a 3,000-character letter, an unlock time and a reply box.

That letter limit holds an 88-word message several times over. Platform-wide, 38.5% of creators password-protect what they share, and both templates offer it at publish. If she would rather skip spooky altogether, the ["I love you" page](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf) earns 29.7% of all views on the site, the most of any template.

## Where a paper card wins, and where a page does

Paper wins if you will see her on 31 October, because she can hold it, prop it on a shelf and keep it for years. No page reproduces your handwriting.

Pages have limits too: English-only screens, no use for inviting a crowd, and little appeal for a screen-averse girlfriend, even though shared pages average 11.1 views. Early on, a 100-word card can feel heavy, so a gift-tag line on a small treat is the gentler size.

## Sources

- Clerc V et al. [Beyond gratitude: a qualitative investigation of compliment letters received by a neonatology service](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12911175). BMC Health Services Research, January 2026.
- Jiang D et al. [Daily positive support and perceived stress during COVID-19 outbreak: the role of daily gratitude within couples](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8053415). Journal of Happiness Studies, April 2021.
- The Public Domain Review. [Halloween Postcards, ca. 1900–1920](https://publicdomainreview.org/collection/halloween-postcards), 29 October 2011.
- United States Postal Service. [Domestic Mail Manual 101, Physical Standards](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/101.htm), postcard and letter rules, read October 2026.
